title: Reference coverage audit (bundle.reference-coverage/v1)
description: Machine-readable comparison of the engine's composition vocabulary against each registered coverage target: stable direct demonstrations and replaceable reference applications remain explicitly distinct roles. Generated by bundle.coverage.reference_coverage_report (CLI: `bundle_run.py coverage --json`). The audit deliberately preserves individual facts: there is no aggregate 'power percentage', because EXERCISED, UNEXERCISED and a launcher policy restriction are not commensurable.

schema.description: Schema identifier, "<name>/v<major>". Consumers reject any value whose name or major differs.

engine_revision.description: Content-addressed identity of engine implementation/configuration source, including the Java Core/Reader/Analyzer sources as well as Python control-plane source. Generated output and the direct demonstration are excluded. The same source revision yields the same value in any checkout location, so two reports are comparable without Git metadata (an extracted tree may have none).

engine_capabilities.description: The engine's composition vocabulary. Cross-checked against the fwgen grammar the Core is verified against: every FW_ name the grammar recognizes is owned by exactly one capability, and every capability's probe token must be accepted by the real parser.

order.description: 1 = first-order (one axis over one sheet's values); 2 = second-order (operates on a prior RESULT TABLE); 3 = consumes a prior brace result, i.e. third order and beyond.

tokens.description: FW_ names this capability owns in the fwgen grammar. Empty for capabilities expressed by syntax rather than a name (the brace forms and size-bounded subset families).

probe.description: A concrete token the engine's own parser must accept, so the registry cannot claim a capability the engine does not parse.

role.description: Architectural role. A direct engine demonstration is not relabelled as a reference application merely because both are measured by this audit.

status.description: Lifecycle status. 'stable' is valid for an engine demonstration; replaceable reference applications use 'reference' or 'experimental'.

specs_unreadable.description: Specifications the engine's own loader rejected. Recorded rather than dropped: a spec that does not parse is a finding, not something to remove from the denominator.

max_composition_order.description: Deepest composition order measured in this application's specifications. A plain brace is order 2; each nested FW_()/FW_()G link consuming the previous brace result adds one.

unexercised_capabilities.description: Supported by the engine, unused by this application. Neither a defect in the application nor a limit of the engine.

policy_restrictions.description: Flags the application's launcher pins, read from its source. Reported separately from capabilities: which capability a pinned --lang or budget ceiling forecloses is not stated by the source and is not guessed here.

value_kind.description: 'literal' = the value is written in the source; 'dynamic' = the flag is passed with a value computed at runtime, so no value is claimed; 'switch' = the flag takes no value.

presence_kind.description: Whether this command-list flag is always present in its builder or only appended on a conditional path.

condition.description: Source expression guarding a conditional flag; empty for an always-present flag.

measurement.description: Present ONLY when a bounded benchmark actually produced measurements on the reporting host. Per-phase seconds are never estimated, extrapolated, or hand-written; an unmeasured phase is absent rather than zero.

phases.description: Phase name -> wall seconds. Engine phases come from the run's own stage records; application phases are the wrapper time measured around the canonical Bundle run.

notes.description: Interpretation limits carried with the data so a consumer cannot read the numbers without them.
